title: Estimated Blood Volume & Maximum Allowable Blood Loss
keywords: premature 95 term 85 infant 80 child 75 adult male 70 female 65
maximum allowable blood loss before transfusion
sources: Gross JB. Anesthesiology 1983 (estimation of allowable blood loss); Miller's Anesthesia — blood-volume estimates by age

changelog.change: Initial entry — weight-based EBV by patient type and the simple ABL formula.

purpose: Estimates the circulating blood volume and the volume of blood that can be lost before the haematocrit falls to the lowest acceptable value — a planning number for when to have product ready and when to transfuse. It is an estimate: reassess against the actual haemodynamics, ongoing loss rate, and a measured haematocrit.

interpretation.label: Have blood products checked and available before loss approaches this volume. As loss nears the ABL, send a haematocrit and start replacing red cells; a restrictive trigger (Hb ~ 7 g/dL, or ~ 8 in active cardiac disease) is appropriate for most stable patients. This estimate assumes iso-volaemic replacement with crystalloid/colloid; brisk or ongoing loss, coagulopathy, or a poor cardiac reserve all move the transfusion point earlier.

notes: The simple formula ABL = EBV × (Hi − Hf) / Hi slightly overestimates; the Gross correction uses the average of the initial and final haematocrit in the denominator. Convert haemoglobin to haematocrit as roughly Hct ≈ 3 × Hb. In children, a small absolute loss is a large fraction of the EBV — weigh sponges and suction and communicate loss early.
buildNote: Formula engine. EBV per kg is a select; ABL uses the simple Gross formula.
